Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD), a data-center and PC chip designer, closed at $508.58, up 13.26%. Oppenheimer's upgrade and Google Cloud's chip selection boosted the shares, while investors are watching AI data-center demand and next week's chip-sector earnings. Trading volume reached 50.7M shares, coming in about 123% above its three-month average of 22.8M shares.

How the markets moved today

The S&P 500 closed at 7,556, up 2.43%, while the Nasdaq Composite finished at 25,253, up 2.74%. Among semiconductor rivals, Nvidia closed at $178.67, down 4.27%, and Intel closed at $59.37, up 5.49%, as chipmakers traded unevenly on AI sentiment and leadership scrutiny.

What this means for investors

On Monday, AMD stock continued to benefit from headwinds following the pullback that began soon after it released its third-quarter 2026 earnings report on Nov. 3.

Oppenheimer upgraded AMD stock to an outperform rating, setting a $600 per share price target. If it meets its target, the chip stock would rise by about 18% from current levels.

Additionally, since AMD's data center segment reported a 97% year-over-year revenue increase in the Q3 report, the company's AI outlook has continued to improve, with guidance for 80% revenue growth next year.

Moreover, AMD announced that its fifth-generation AMD EPYC CPUs power Alphabet's Google Cloud's TPU 8tx, establishing hardware-enforced confidential computing for that company's cloud AI systems.

Furthermore, with the notable exception of Nvidia, most chip stocks rose in Monday trading. Nvidia, AMD's strongest competitor in its data center business, faces uncertainty amid an indiscretion involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and an alleged Chinese spy.

The implications of such an act have ripple effects across the industry. Although it remains unclear whether, or to what extent, potential changes at Nvidia would affect AMD stock, AMD seemed to benefit from investors fleeing the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia.

AMD rose 13% to $508.58 at Monday's close, nearly $100 billion of market value, on Oppenheimer's upgrade to Outperform with a $600 target and a Google Cloud TPU 8tx host win; Nvidia fell 4.3% on the Huang investigation.

A retiree's 1,000 shares bought at $55.94 in October 2022 gained $59,540 Monday and $104,180 in two sessions; the position is now 21% of a $2.4 million portfolio, up from 10% at the end of 2025.

Selling 265 shares now and 265 in January trims AMD to 10%, costs $31,699 in federal tax over two years ($6,286 less than one sale), keeps the 3.8% NIIT at zero and holds the Medicare surcharge to $1,949 a year.

Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor)

Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) has won back everything Thursday's 17% crash took, and more. The stock closed up 13% at $508.58 on Monday, adding nearly $100 billion in market value, after Oppenheimer upgraded it to Outperform with a $600 price target and AMD said its EPYC processors will run the host side of Google Cloud's new TPU 8tx systems. The same morning Nvidia fell as much as 8.8% and closed down 4.3%, a drop worth about $192 billion of market value, a day after its board opened an independent investigation into reports about chief executive Jensen Huang.

Lisa Su, AMD's chair and chief executive, had spent Thursday watching her stock fall 17.26% to $404.40 in the worst day for chip stocks since 2020. Asked about it on Yahoo Finance that afternoon, she said: "I think the market can sometimes be a little bit short-sighted. It is what it is." Two sessions later the stock is up 25.8% from that close and back above the $488.78 it closed at before the crash.

title: Analyzing AMD as a near-term beneficiary of Nvidia’s leadership uncertainty

Analyzing AMD as a near-term beneficiary of Nvidia’s leadership uncertainty
Investing.com

AMD
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investing.com -- The tape suggests investors are already treating Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) as a relative winner. It trades at $513.73 (+14.41%) as of Nov 9, 3:38 PM EST. NVIDIA (NVDA) is at $177.20 (-5.06%) at the same time. That's a roughly 19-point gap in one session. AMD is also up about 134% YTD but down 15.6% over the past month, so it isn't a clean one-way run.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

What's hanging over Nvidia

Board probe: Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang over his relationship with a woman U.S. officials believe was a Chinese intelligence asset. Huang admitted an affair Read more (Nov 9, 2026).

Key-person risk: Bernstein notes Huang has about 60 direct reports and that it's unclear who would step in. It expects the overhang to last a while, but kept its Outperform rating and $400 target Read more (Nov 9, 2026).

Regulatory angle: Citi flags governance, export-control compliance on H200 chips going to China (Read more (Nov 9, 2026).

Earnings timing: Nvidia reports on Nov 17, just as congressional scrutiny builds Read more (Nov 9, 2026).

The AMD bull case

An NH Investment & Securities analyst said rivals including AMD could draw more attention in the short term. Samsung, which has close ties to AMD, could also benefit Read more (Nov 9, 2026). If probe delays or product-launch slippage materialize at Nvidia, AMD is the obvious alternative for customers building AI capacity. Money rotating out of Nvidia may also be flowing into AMD.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

The bear case

Sentiment, not fundamentals: No coverage found says Nvidia has lost customers or orders. Nvidia says it will continue "without interruption."

Shared risk: The AI-spending worries behind Nvidia's weakness, such as hyperscaler capex sustainability and valuation, also apply to AMD. Tighter export rules or antitrust rules for AI data centers would hit both.

Crowded move: A 14% one-day gain after a fall of about 15.6% in a month can reverse quickly if the probe turns out to be benign.

Bernstein's warning: It said the main beneficiary of Huang's removal "would clearly be China." That points to sector-wide disruption more than a clean handoff to AMD.

Bottom line

AMD is a near-term sentiment beneficiary, and the price action shows it. A lasting share gain would need real evidence, such as Nvidia product delays, customer diversification or leadership changes. Nvidia's Nov 17 earnings and the board probe's findings are the next tests.
